card.name: Justice

upright.text: Equity, rightness, probity, executive; triumph of the deserving side in law.

reversed.text: Law in all its departments, legal complications, bigotry, bias, excessive severity.

position.label: What covers him
position.role: General influence or atmosphere affecting the matter.

direct_component.text: It is a card of valour, for, on the surface, six are attacking one, who has, however, the vantage position. On the intellectual plane, it signifies discussion, wordy strife; in business—negotiations, war of trade, barter, competition. It is further a card of success, for the combatant is on the top and his enemies may be unable to reach him.

overall.summary: The central atmosphere (valour;discussion;competition) meets the crossing motif (attraction;love;trials overcome). Compare the aim (announcements;indecision) with the established basis (injustice;double dealing),then read the passing and approaching influences in order. The right-hand staff moves from stance through environment and hopes/fears to a symbolic culmination (prudence;discernment;accomplishment). This is a compositional reading,not a forecast or a source-documented card-pair rule.

celtic_procedure.significator: Explicit user-selected person/matter card,face up and removed from pack;no automatic age,sex,appearance or temperament classification.
celtic_procedure.facing: Caller must select left/right before draw;diagram p305 faces left with5 on right and6 on left. Opposite facing mirrors5/6 only;right-side staff stays right.
celtic_procedure.digital_convention: Three Fisher-Yates shuffle/nonempty-cut rounds implement a named digital reading of shuffle and cut three times;not a replication of physical ritual.

exceptions.rule: A favourable crossing card can mean minor obstacles or something good that is unhelpful in this context;do not universally negate its meaning.
